purpose: Bevacizumab-maly is used to treat certain types of cancer, including colorectal cancer, lung cancer, kidney cancer, cervical cancer, and some brain tumors. It is also used for a type of eye condition called wet age-related macular degeneration in some cases. It is often given along with other cancer medicines to help them work better.
how_it_works: Your body sometimes grows new blood vessels that feed tumors and help them grow — this medicine blocks a protein called VEGF that signals your body to make those new blood vessels. By cutting off the tumor's blood supply, it helps slow or stop cancer growth. Think of it like turning off the water supply to a weed so it cannot survive.
common_side_effects: High blood pressure, tiredness, headache, loss of appetite, diarrhea, nausea, mouth sores, dry or runny nose, back pain, and taste changes are common. You may also notice slower wound healing than usual.
warnings: This medicine can cause serious bleeding, including internal bleeding — tell your doctor right away if you cough up blood or notice unusual bleeding. It can also cause a hole to form in the stomach or intestines (called perforation), serious blood clots, stroke, heart problems, and very high blood pressure. It must be stopped well before any surgery because it slows healing. It can harm an unborn baby, so reliable birth control is very important during treatment and for several months after.
typical_dosing: This medicine is given through an IV (intravenous infusion) at a clinic or hospital — you will not inject it yourself at home. The dose and how often you receive it depends on the type of cancer being treated, your weight, and what other medicines you are taking. Common schedules are every 2 weeks or every 3 weeks, and each infusion can take 30 to 90 minutes. Your doctor will determine the exact dose that is right for you.
